title: Cancore filler protocol v1 — REST fallback
$comment: protocol §3.6. Bodies are the WebSocket frames: every request body is a filler message with its envelope (id, fillerId, sentAt) and msgSig, verified before processing as on the WebSocket (S-19); every response is a freshly signed S→F message. Login: GET /v1/filler/auth/challenge?fillerId= returns a signed auth.challenge addressed to that fillerId; POST /v1/filler/auth with the auth.response (FillerAuth over it) returns {token, expiresAt}. The challenge route is anonymous and its refusals are UNSIGNED (unsignedErrorBody, no sig, nothing journalled): 400 BAD_REQUEST — fillerId missing or not a fillerId; 404 UNKNOWN_REQUEST — fillerId unknown or not ACTIVE; 429 RATE_LIMITED with retryAfterMs and a Retry-After header — the login rate class of that fillerId is over its limit. POST /v1/filler/auth refuses UNSIGNED too as long as it has checked no signature: 400 BAD_REQUEST — no or a malformed fillerId; 404 UNKNOWN_REQUEST — fillerId unknown or not ACTIVE; 401 UNAUTHENTICATED — the fillerId holds no live challenge (evicted, expired or used: ask for a new one); 429 RATE_LIMITED (retryAfterMs, Retry-After). Its refusals after the signature checks (BAD_SIGNATURE, STALE_MESSAGE, REPLAYED_MESSAGE, UNSUPPORTED_VERSION, NOT_ELIGIBLE, UNAUTHENTICATED) are the signed error. The other /v1/filler/* routes need `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the token is bound to (fillerId, message key) and stops working when it expires, when the message key is changed, or when the filler is no longer ACTIVE. The same token opens the WebSocket (asyncapi.json: offered as the subprotocol bearer.<token>). A ticket of another filler is 404 UNKNOWN_TICKET. Rate limits are per fillerId, shared by REST and every WebSocket session of it: over the limit a bearer route answers 429 with an UNSIGNED unsignedErrorBody {type: error, code: RATE_LIMITED, message, retryAfterMs} and a Retry-After header (seconds, rounded up), journals nothing one by one, and the request changes nothing; during the cooldown after sustained excess every bearer route answers so. Every 429 is unsigned, on every route; a filler decides by the status and takes retryAfterMs (else Retry-After) as a hint. Every other non-2xx of a bearer route is the signed error. GET /v1/filler/attestations/{orderHash} answers 404 ATTESTATIONS_NOT_READY until the gateway holds ≥ threshold verified signatures for this filler's fill, and 404 UNKNOWN_TICKET when this filler holds no ticket on the order. /v1/draws/* and /v1/gateway are public. Every non-2xx body is the signed `error` frame, with the HTTP status of x-error-status — except a 429 (always unsignedErrorBody) and the unsigned refusals of an endpoint that names an errorBody. x-endpoints: request/query/response/errorBody name a $def here or in messages.schema.json.

unsignedErrorBody.description: An unsigned refusal: every 429, and the refusals of the login routes decided before any signature check. Not signed, not addressed, nothing journalled; a filler cannot verify it and treats it as a hint only (status, code, retryAfterMs)

retryAfterMs.description: with RATE_LIMITED (429): ms until the rate class may be used again

fillerId.description: the filler logging in; the challenge is addressed to it and answerable only by it

empty.description: no fields in v1; receivers ignore unknown ones (V-2)

status.description: a request filter: the gateway owns the list, so it is closed

stakeBindingRequest.description: sig = StakeBinding{partnerId, stakingAddress, chainId, nonce} by the staking address; the body carries the filler envelope and msgSig like every request body
